name: Slack
summary: Creating a Slack app and running the v2 OAuth flow is self-serve and documented. Getting scopes approved for apps published to other workspaces involves Slack's review; the docs checked here do not state how long that takes.
difficultyWhy: Setup is simple, but redirect URL rules, additive scopes and the review path for published apps add real surface area.

time.wait: None for unlisted distribution; Marketplace review time is not published

approval.details: Installing to your own workspace needs no review. The docs mention an unapproved_scope error when scopes are still in review or were never submitted for review, which implies a review path for published apps. The full process was not described on the fetched page.

requirements.text: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor; configure them under OAuth & Permissions.
A redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured URL. With multiple URLs configured, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and access steps or you get bad_redirect_uri.
Use 'scope' for bot scopes and 'user_scope' for user scopes. Sign in with Slack user scopes must go in a separate flow.
The temporary code expires after ten minutes; verify 'state' on return.
Scopes are additive on reinstall and cannot be removed without revoking the token.
Tokens do not expire on their own unless token rotation is enabled (available to apps with granular permissions).

To install in other workspaces, you need an OAuth flow, SSL on all redirect/interaction/events URLs, and must activate 'Public Distribution' under Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces. Slack calls this unlisted distribution and it does not require Marketplace review.
Some workspaces require admin approval for app installs, so request only the permissions you need. Slack recommends Marketplace listing for commercial apps.

steps.title: Create the app in Slack's app management console
steps.detail: Create a new app (from scratch or manifest) under the workspace you will use for development.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs. HTTPS only. Add every environment.

steps.title: Pick the minimum bot and user scopes
steps.detail: Mark nice-to-have scopes as optional so users can decline them, and handle missing_scope errors.

steps.title: Send users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize
steps.detail: Include client_id, scope/user_scope, redirect_uri and a random state.

steps.title: Exchange the code with oauth.v2.access
steps.detail: Do this within ten minutes. Store tokens per workspace.

steps.title: If publishing broadly, submit scopes/app for review
steps.detail: Plan for an unknown wait. Check the current Marketplace guidelines directly with Slack.

blockers.fix: Send the identical redirect_uri in both the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls when more than one URL is configured.
A requested scope is still in review or was never submitted. Submit it for review or remove it from the request.

blockers.issue: missing_scope after user declines an optional scope
blockers.fix: Handle gracefully and re-prompt only when the feature is used.

agentCan: Generate the authorize URL and token exchange code.
Implement state checking and per-workspace token storage.
developerMust: Create the app while signed in to Slack and pick the workspace.
Own any Marketplace/scope review submission and correspondence.
uncertain: Marketplace/scope review duration and requirements: the Marketplace review guide URL I tried returned 404, so this was not verified.
App creation steps (new app from scratch or manifest) come from general knowledge, not the fetched pages.

meta.tested: Read the primary docs page. The old api.slack.com URL redirects (302) to docs.slack.dev. No app was created.
